plainFields.description: Shop name as it appeared at the time of snapshot creation. This is the primary business identifier that customers see when browsing products and making purchases.

plainFields.name: shop_description
plainFields.description: Shop description explaining the seller's business, values, and product offerings as displayed to customers at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: logo_image_url
plainFields.description: URL to the seller's logo image used for visual branding and customer recognition at the time of snapshot creation.

plainFields.name: snapshot_number
plainFields.description: Sequential version number of this snapshot within the seller's profile history. Increments with each profile modification to establish chronological order.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Exact date and time when this snapshot was created, recording when the profile modification occurred.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations
models.description:
Tracks seller registration requests submitted by users before administrative approval.

This table stores initial seller registration data including shop name and description that users submit when requesting to become sellers on the platform. Each registration goes through an approval workflow where administrators review and decide whether to approve or reject the request. Approved registrations result in the creation of a seller account in the {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers} table and a seller profile in {@link ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles}.

The registration has lifecycle statuses: pending (awaiting review), approved, rejected, and withdrawn. Status transitions are tracked in the separate {@link ecommerce_mall_seller_registration_status_histories} table for audit purposes. Each user can have only one pending registration at a time, but may have multiple historical registrations with different statuses.

This table is subsidiary to the user entity since registrations are submitted by and managed through user accounts.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who submitted this seller registration request. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: Requested shop name for the seller's business. This name will be used for the seller's public shop profile if approved. Must be unique among active shops.

plainFields.name: shop_description
plainFields.description: Description of the seller's business, products, and shop concept. Provides context for administrators during approval review.

plainFields.name: current_status
plainFields.description: Current status of the registration request. Values: pending (awaiting review), approved (administrator approved), rejected (administrator rejected), withdrawn (user cancelled). Derived from the latest status history entry.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user submitted this registration request.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this registration record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this registration record was soft deleted. Allows for audit trail preservation while removing from active queries.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_payment_accounts
models.description:
Seller payment account details for receiving payouts from sales.

Stores secure payment information including bank account details, digital wallet addresses, or payment gateway integration credentials. Each seller can have multiple payment accounts but only one can be active at a time for receiving payouts.

Payment accounts undergo verification processes before being activated for payouts. Account details are stored with appropriate security measures to protect sensitive financial information.

All account modifications are tracked for audit purposes, and deleted accounts are soft-deleted to maintain historical payout records. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller who owns this payment account. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: payment_method_type
plainFields.description: Type of payment method: 'bank_account', 'digital_wallet', 'payment_gateway', or 'card'.

plainFields.name: account_identifier
plainFields.description: Secure identifier for the payment account (masked account number, wallet address, or gateway token).

plainFields.name: account_holder_name
plainFields.description: Name of the account holder as registered with the payment provider.

plainFields.name: routing_details
plainFields.description: Additional routing information such as bank routing number, BIC/SWIFT code, or wallet network.

plainFields.name: verification_status
plainFields.description: Current verification status: 'pending_verification', 'verified', 'suspended', or 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: is_primary
plainFields.description: Indicates if this is the primary payment account for receiving payouts.

plainFields.name: last_payout_date
plainFields.description: Date of the most recent successful payout to this account.

plainFields.name: verification_notes
plainFields.description: Administrator notes regarding account verification, including rejection reasons if applicable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payment account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payment account was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payment account was soft-deleted. Null indicates active account.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_approvals
models.description:
Tracks the seller approval workflow including status changes, rejection reasons, and administrator decisions.

This table records the complete history of a seller's approval journey from initial registration through potential rejections and re-submissions to final approval. Each record represents a specific status transition in the approval process, allowing administrators to track decision timelines and sellers to understand their approval status.

When a seller first registers, an initial 'pending' record is created. Administrators can then approve or reject the seller, recording their decision and any rejection reason. If rejected, sellers can submit a new registration request, creating additional approval records. Approved sellers have a final 'approved' record that grants them selling privileges.

{@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id} identifies the seller being approved, while {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id} identifies the administrator who made the decision (null for pending status).

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller being approved. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who approved or rejected the seller. Null when status is pending. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current approval status: 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation provided by administrator when rejecting a seller registration. Required when status is 'rejected', null otherwise.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this approval record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this approval record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this approval record was soft-deleted. Null indicates active record.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_registration_status_histories
models.description:
Tracks status history and timestamps for seller registration requests, separating temporal data from core registration entity.

Each record captures a specific status transition in the seller registration approval workflow, including the status change timestamp and optional reason for status changes. This historical tracking enables audit trails of registration decisions and supports seller approval process transparency.

Status transitions follow the seller registration lifecycle: pending (initial submission), approved (administrator approval), or rejected (administrator rejection with reason). Multiple history records may exist for the same registration if sellers resubmit after rejection.

{@link ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_registration_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller registration request being tracked. {@link ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations.id}

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Registration status at this point in time. Values: 'pending' (awaiting review), 'approved' (registration accepted), 'rejected' (registration denied).

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional explanation for status changes, particularly important for rejection reasons to inform sellers why their registration was denied.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status history record was created, marking when the registration status changed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status history record was last updated. Rarely changes as status history records are largely immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status history record was soft-deleted. Allows for audit trail preservation while supporting data privacy requirements.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_categories
models.description:
Main category table storing all product categories and subcategories with hierarchical relationships.

Categories serve as logical product groupings for marketplace organization, supporting one-level nesting of subcategories within parent categories. Each category includes a name, description, and status to control visibility and lifecycle. Categories are exclusively managed by platform administrators for consistent product classification.

Subcategories inherit the organizational structure of parent categories while providing more specific product grouping. The hierarchical relationship enables efficient navigation from broad product categories to specific subcategories.

{@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id} as creator and modifier for administrator management tracking.
{@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id} for parent-child relationships enabling one-level subcategory nesting.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent category for hierarchical nesting. References parent category's {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}. Null for top-level categories.

foreignFields.name: created_by
foreignFields.description: Administrator who created this category. References {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: updated_by
foreignFields.description: Administrator who last modified this category. References {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name for product classification. Must be clear and descriptive for customer navigation.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description explaining the category scope and included product types.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Category lifecycle status. Active categories are visible in product listings, Archived categories are hidden but preserved, Deleted categories are soft-deleted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was soft-deleted. Null for active categories.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_category_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshots of category changes, preserving previous states for audit trails.

Created automatically whenever categories are modified, archived, or deleted by administrators. This table serves as an immutable audit trail that captures the complete state of a category at specific points in time, including all fields such as name, description, status, and parent relationships.

Each snapshot records which administrator made the change and when it occurred, providing full traceability for category management operations. These records are preserved even if the original category is deleted, maintaining compliance with the platform's Snapshot Principle for financial transparency.

{@link ecommerce_mall_categories} for the current category state.
{@link ecommerce_mall_administrators} for administrator information.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_category_id
foreignFields.description: The category that was snapshotted. {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who made the change that triggered the snapshot. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name as it existed at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Category description as it existed at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Category status at snapshot time. Must be one of: 'Active', 'Archived', 'Deleted'.

plainFields.name: parent_category_name
plainFields.description: Name of parent category at snapshot time, denormalized for historical reference. Null if category was top-level.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Represents the exact moment the category state was captured.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was last updated. Typically null for immutable snapshots.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was soft-deleted. Allows for audit trail preservation while supporting data retention policies.

plainFields.name: change_reason
plainFields.description: Optional reason for the change that triggered this snapshot, provided by the administrator.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_uncategorized_products
models.description:
Tracks products that have become uncategorized due to category deletion, enabling administrators to reclassify them properly.

When a category is deleted (status changed to 'Deleted'), all products previously classified under that category become uncategorized. This table captures those products with references to the deleted category for historical context. Administrators can later review this list and reassign products to appropriate active categories.

Each record represents a single product that needs reclassification. The product remains in this table until an administrator assigns it to a new category, at which point the reclassified_at timestamp is set and the administrator responsible is recorded.

This table ensures no products are lost in classification limbo and provides an audit trail of category deletion impacts on product organization. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}, {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}, {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: The product that became uncategorized. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: The category that was deleted, causing the product to become uncategorized. This is a historical reference to the category at the time of deletion. {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who reclassified the product into a new category, if reclassification has occurred. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the product became uncategorized due to category deletion.

plainFields.name: reclassified_at
plainFields.description: When the product was reclassified into a new category by an administrator. Null indicates the product is still awaiting reclassification.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_products
models.description:
Main product entity containing core product information like name, description, category, base price, and seller reference.

Products represent sellable items in the marketplace that belong to specific sellers and are classified under categories. Each product can have multiple variants (different SKUs) and images. The product record includes essential metadata for display, search, and filtering.

Whenever a product is edited, a snapshot {@link ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots} must be created to preserve the previous state as required by the Snapshot Principle for financial audit trails. This ensures that customers see the exact product state at the time of purchase.

Products can exist in different statuses: draft (unpublished), published (available for purchase), archived (hidden but preserved), and deleted (soft-deleted with preservation).

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who owns this product. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Category classification for product organization. {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}

plainFields.name: product_code
plainFields.description: Seller-defined unique product code for internal reference and tracking. Must be unique within the seller's product catalog.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Product name displayed to customers in listings and detail pages. Should be descriptive and searchable.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed product description including features, specifications, and usage information. Supports rich text formatting.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: Base price for the product in the marketplace currency. Individual variants may override this with specific prices.

plainFields.name: product_status
plainFields.description: Current lifecycle status of the product. Allowed values: 'draft' (unpublished), 'published' (available for purchase), 'archived' (hidden from listings), 'deleted' (soft-deleted).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was initially created by the seller.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was last modified. Updates on any field change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was soft-deleted. Null indicates the product is active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variants
models.description:
Product variants representing specific configurations with unique SKU codes, option values, price overrides, and stock tracking.

Each variant belongs to exactly one product and can have multiple option values (e.g., color, size) that define its specific configuration. The SKU code must be unique across all variants. Variants can override the parent product's base price and maintain their own stock quantity, which is managed through inventory records rather than direct updates.

Variants support soft deletion to preserve historical references in orders and snapshots. When deleted, they become unavailable for new purchases but remain visible in historical contexts. All variant modifications trigger snapshot creation in the {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots} table to maintain audit trails as required by the Snapshot Principle.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged product's {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: sku
plainFields.description: Stock Keeping Unit code uniquely identifying this variant across the platform. Used for inventory management, order processing, and supplier references.

plainFields.name: price_override
plainFields.description: Optional variant-specific price that overrides the parent product's base price. When null, the parent product's base price applies to this variant.

plainFields.name: stock_quantity
plainFields.description: Current available stock quantity for this variant. Updated through inventory records rather than direct modifications. Zero indicates out of stock.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this variant was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this variant was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this variant was soft deleted. Null indicates active variant.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_images
models.description:
Product images supporting multiple images per product with ordering and thumbnail designation.

Sellers can upload multiple images for their products to create product galleries. The first image in the ordered sequence serves as the main thumbnail image displayed in product listings. Images can be reordered by sellers to control gallery presentation, and images can be deleted when no longer needed.

Image changes are captured in product snapshots via {@link ecommerce_mall_product_snapshot_images} to preserve historical states for audit trails. Each image belongs to exactly one product through {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

Images are stored as URIs pointing to external storage services, allowing scalable image hosting separate from the database. The order field determines display sequence in product galleries.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Parent product this image belongs to. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: uri
plainFields.description: Image URI pointing to the stored image file location. Supports external storage services for scalable image hosting.

plainFields.name: order
plainFields.description: Display order within the product gallery. Lower values appear first. The image with order 0 serves as the main thumbnail image.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this image was uploaded to the product.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this image was last modified (reordered).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this image was deleted. Null indicates the image is active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_inventory_records
models.description:
Inventory history records tracking all stock changes for variants with reasons and timestamps.

Each record represents a single change in stock quantity, providing a complete audit trail of all inventory movements. Positive quantity changes indicate stock increases (restocking, cancellation refunds), while negative quantity changes indicate stock decreases (order placements, adjustments). The current stock for a variant is calculated by summing all quantity changes for that variant.

These records serve as an immutable audit trail for inventory transparency, enabling sellers to track stock movements and administrators to verify inventory activities. Records cannot be modified or deleted once created, ensuring a non-repudiable history for dispute resolution and regulatory compliance.

Linked to {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants} to track stock changes per specific variant configuration.

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: The specific product variant whose stock changed. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}

plainFields.name: quantity_change
plainFields.description: Amount of stock added or removed. Positive values indicate stock increases (restocking, cancellation refunds), negative values indicate stock decreases (order placements, adjustments).

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Explanation of why the inventory change occurred. Common reasons include 'restock', 'order placement', 'cancellation refund', 'refund processing', 'adjustment loss', or 'system correction'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the inventory change was recorded. Automatically set to the exact moment the record is created, ensuring accurate chronological ordering of inventory events.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When the record was last updated by the system for internal tracking purposes.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots capturing complete product state at specific points in time for audit trails and historical preservation.

Whenever a product is edited or modified, a snapshot is created that preserves all product fields (name, description, category, base price) as they existed before the change. This table serves as the foundation for the platform's financial transparency requirements, ensuring that customers, sellers, and administrators can reference exactly what was displayed at any historical moment.

Each snapshot links to variant snapshots captured at the same moment through {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots.snapshot_id} and image snapshots through {@link ecommerce_mall_product_snapshot_images.snapshot_id}. The denormalized data structure allows historical queries without complex joins to reconstruct past product states.

Snapshots are created automatically by the system during product edits and are never modified or deleted, maintaining a complete audit trail for dispute resolution, compliance verification, and customer confidence in marketplace transactions.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: The product that was captured in this snapshot. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller who owned the product at snapshot time. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: The product's category at snapshot time. {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Product name as it existed at snapshot time. Preserved exactly as displayed to customers.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Product description as it existed at snapshot time. Preserved exactly as displayed to customers.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: Product base price as it existed at snapshot time, in the platform's base currency.

plainFields.name: snapshot_reason
plainFields.description: Optional explanation of why this snapshot was created, such as 'product edit', 'price change', or 'category update'. Provides context for historical analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Represents the exact moment when the product state was captured.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was last updated. For snapshots, this typically matches created_at as snapshots are immutable.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was soft-deleted. Snapshots are never deleted, so this should remain null to maintain complete audit trail.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots
models.description:
Variant snapshots preserving variant details (SKU, options, price, and stock quantity) at specific points in time, linked to product snapshots.

Each record represents the complete state of a product variant at the moment a product snapshot was created. This includes the SKU code, price, stock quantity, and option values (stored in the separate ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot_options table). These snapshots are immutable and serve as audit trails for financial transparency and dispute resolution, especially important for order items where the exact variant configuration at purchase time must be preserved.

The snapshot references both the original variant ({@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}) for lineage tracking and the parent product snapshot ({@link ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots.id}) to maintain the complete product state context.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent product snapshot that this variant snapshot belongs to. The product snapshot captures the complete product state including all variant snapshots at a specific point in time. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original product variant that was snapshotted. This maintains lineage and allows tracking of changes to the same variant over time. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: SKU code of the variant at the time of snapshot creation. This is preserved exactly as it was configured in the original variant and is used for inventory tracking and order item reference.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Price of the variant at the time of snapshot creation. For order items, this price is preserved for the purchased quantity and used for financial calculations and refunds.

plainFields.name: stock_at_snapshot
plainFields.description: Stock quantity of the variant at the exact moment of snapshot creation. This captures the inventory level and is important for audit trails and inventory discrepancy resolution.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this variant snapshot was created. This marks the exact moment when the variant state was captured for historical preservation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this variant snapshot was last updated. Note: Variant snapshots are generally immutable, but this field exists for system consistency and potential metadata updates.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_snapshot_images
models.description:
Immutable snapshots of product images captured at the time of product snapshot creation.

When a product snapshot is created (due to product edits), this table preserves the exact state of all product images including their URLs, ordering positions, and any captions. Each record represents a single image as it existed at the snapshot moment, maintaining the gallery configuration for audit trails and historical reference.

This table supports the Snapshot Principle requirement for financial transparency, ensuring that product image changes are tracked alongside other product modifications. Images are captured in their exact order at snapshot time, allowing reconstruction of the product's visual presentation for any historical point.

{@link ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots.id}

foreignFields.name: product_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent product snapshot containing this image. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots.id}

plainFields.name: image_url
plainFields.description: URL of the product image as it existed at snapshot time. This preserves the exact image location and content visible to customers when the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: order_index
plainFields.description: Position of this image within the product's gallery at snapshot time. Lower numbers indicate earlier positions (e.g., 0 for primary/thumbnail image). Preserves the exact visual presentation order.

plainFields.name: caption
plainFields.description: Optional descriptive text associated with the image at snapshot time. May include alt text, product feature descriptions, or contextual information.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this image snapshot was created (matches parent snapshot creation time).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this image snapshot was last updated (typically matches creation time for immutable snapshots).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot_options
models.description:
Option key-value pairs for product variant snapshots, preserving the exact option configuration at snapshot time.

When a product variant snapshot is created (during product edits), this table stores all option values that defined the variant at that moment, such as color, size, material, or other product-specific attributes. Each option is stored as a separate key-value pair to maintain atomic values and support flexible attribute structures across different product types.

These records are immutable once created and serve as part of the complete audit trail for product changes. The options preserved here are referenced when reconstructing the historical state of a product variant for dispute resolution, customer service inquiries, or regulatory compliance.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent variant snapshot containing these option values. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots.id}.

plainFields.name: option_key
plainFields.description: The option attribute name (e.g., 'color', 'size', 'material', 'weight'). This represents the type of option being configured for the product variant.

plainFields.name: option_value
plainFields.description: The specific value for this option (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton', '500g'). This preserves the exact configuration that was available to customers at the time of snapshot creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this option value was recorded as part of the variant snapshot. This matches the parent snapshot creation time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last updated. For immutable snapshot data, this should typically match created_at.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons
models.description: Predefined reasons for inventory adjustments like restocking, order fulfillment, returns, or loss. These standardized reasons categorize stock changes for reporting, analytics, and audit purposes. Each reason has a code for internal reference and a display name for user interfaces. {@link ecommerce_mall_inventory_records.adjustment_reason_id}

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Unique internal code for the adjustment reason. Used for programmatic reference and API operations.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User-friendly name shown in interfaces for selecting adjustment reasons.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of when to use this adjustment reason and its business context.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this adjustment reason is available for selection. Inactive reasons are hidden from current selections but preserved for historical records.

plainFields.name: category
plainFields.description: Broad category grouping similar adjustment reasons. Examples: 'restocking', 'order_processing', 'returns', 'loss_adjustment'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this adjustment reason was added to the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this adjustment reason was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this adjustment reason was soft-deleted. Null indicates the reason is active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options
models.description:
Stores option name-value pairs for product variants in a normalized structure.

Each record represents a single option configuration for a product variant, such as color: 'Red' or size: 'Large'. This table enables flexible variant configuration without using JSON fields, supporting any number of options per variant while maintaining data integrity.

Options are managed through the parent product variant and cannot be independently created or searched. The ordering field allows sellers to control display sequence of options on product pages.

{@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Parent product variant that this option belongs to. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: option_name
plainFields.description: Name of the option such as 'color', 'size', 'material', or 'style'. Used to group related option values.

plainFields.name: option_value
plainFields.description: Value of the option such as 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton', or 'Classic'. Represents the specific selection for this option name.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Order in which this option should be displayed relative to other options for the same variant. Lower numbers appear first.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this option was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this option was last modified.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_wishlists
models.description:
Tracks customer product interests for future consideration, automatically removes deleted products.

Each wishlist entry represents a customer's interest in a specific product for potential future purchase. Customers can add products to their wishlist to track items they're interested in but not ready to purchase immediately. When a product is deleted by its seller, all associated wishlist entries are automatically removed through foreign key cascade constraints.

Wishlist entries are managed independently by customers through add, remove, and view operations. The system ensures duplicate prevention through unique constraints on customer-product combinations.

Related entities: {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id} for customer ownership, {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id} for product reference.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who added the product to their wishlist. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product that the customer is interested in. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was added to the customer's wishlist.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the wishlist entry was last modified (typically same as created_at since wishlist entries are not edited).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the wishlist entry was removed by the customer or automatically due to product deletion. Null indicates active wishlist entry.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts
models.description:
Persistent customer shopping cart for pre-purchase item assembly with total price calculation.

Each registered customer has exactly one active shopping cart that serves as a temporary holding area for product variants before checkout. The cart automatically combines quantities when the same variant is added multiple times, calculates subtotals for each line item, and provides a running total of all items.

Shopping carts bridge the browsing experience to the purchase commitment by allowing customers to assemble items from multiple sellers, adjust quantities, and review the total price before proceeding to checkout. {@link ecommerce_mall_customer_profiles.id} own their shopping carts, while {@link ecommerce_mall_cart_items.id} represent the individual line items within the cart.

Deleted carts are soft-deleted to preserve historical data while removing them from active customer interactions.

foreignFields.name: customer_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Owning customer's profile reference. Each customer has exactly one active shopping cart for pre-purchase item assembly. {@link ecommerce_mall_customer_profiles.id}.

plainFields.name: total_price
plainFields.description: Calculated total price of all items in the cart, representing the sum of all cart item subtotals (price × quantity). This value is updated whenever cart items are added, removed, or modified.

plainFields.name: item_count
plainFields.description: Total number of distinct product variants in the cart, counting each variant once regardless of quantity. Used for quick display of cart size without loading all cart items.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the shopping cart was first created for the customer, typically during initial account setup or first product addition.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the shopping cart was last modified, including any changes to cart items, quantities, or pricing calculations.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the shopping cart was soft-deleted, preserving historical data while removing the cart from active customer interactions. Null indicates an active cart.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_cart_items
models.description:
Variant-specific lines within customer shopping carts with quantity management and automatic combination of duplicate variants.

Each cart item represents a specific product variant added to a shopping cart, with a quantity and price reference. The system automatically combines quantities when the same variant is added multiple times. Cart items belong to a parent shopping cart and reference the specific product variant being purchased.

Business rules: 1) The same variant cannot appear multiple times in the same cart - quantities are combined, 2) Cart items are removed from cart when checkout completes, 3) Cart items become unavailable when variant stock is insufficient or variant is deleted.

foreignFields.name: shopping_cart_id
foreignFields.description: Parent shopping cart that contains this cart item. {@link ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Specific product variant being added to cart. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units of this variant in the cart. When same variant is added multiple times, quantities are combined into this single field.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart item was first added to the cart.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart item was last modified (quantity changed or refreshed).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart item was removed from the cart (soft delete). Null while still active in cart.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_wishlist_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots of wishlist changes for audit trails, preserving previous states when products are added or removed.

This table records each addition or removal event for products in customer wishlists, creating a complete audit trail of wishlist modifications. Each snapshot captures the wishlist entry state at the time of change, including the customer, product, and timestamp of the event. Snapshots are created whenever a product is added to or removed from a wishlist, ensuring compliance with the platform's Snapshot Principle requirement for financial transparency and dispute resolution.

These records serve as historical evidence for customer preferences, support dispute resolution regarding product availability claims, and enable analytics on wishlist behavior patterns. {@link ecommerce_mall_wishlists.id} represents the parent wishlist entity, while {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id} and {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id} provide direct references to the involved actors and catalog items.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_wishlist_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent wishlist entity. {@link ecommerce_mall_wishlists.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Denormalized reference to the customer who owns the wishlist. Improves query performance for customer history analysis. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product that was added or removed from the wishlist. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Type of wishlist change event. 'added' indicates the product was added to the wishlist, 'removed' indicates the product was removed from the wishlist.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, representing when the wishlist change occurred.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was last updated. For immutable snapshots, this equals created_at but is included for consistency with temporal field patterns.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shopping_cart_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots of shopping cart changes for audit trails, preserving cart states before modifications.

This table implements the Snapshot Principle for shopping cart operations. Whenever a shopping cart is created, updated, or emptied, a snapshot is automatically created to preserve the complete cart state at that moment. Each snapshot includes the cart contents, pricing, and metadata, enabling full audit trails for dispute resolution and historical analysis.

Snapshots are immutable records that cannot be modified or deleted. They capture the exact cart state before any modification, including all items, quantities, and prices. The snapshot_data field preserves the complete cart structure for historical reference. {@link ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts} is the parent cart being snapshotted, and {@link ecommerce_mall_customers} identifies who triggered the snapshot.

Snapshots are essential for financial transparency and customer support, allowing administrators to reconstruct cart states at any point in time for order disputes or system audits.

foreignFields.name: shopping_cart_id
foreignFields.description: The shopping cart being snapshotted. This immutable reference preserves which cart state was captured at this moment. {@link ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts.id}

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who triggered the snapshot. This records which actor initiated the cart change that caused this snapshot. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: snapshot_type
plainFields.description:
Type of snapshot event that occurred. Indicates what operation triggered the snapshot creation.

Allowed values:
- 'cart_created': Initial cart creation
- 'cart_updated': Cart contents modified (items added/removed, quantities changed)
- 'cart_emptied': All items removed from cart
- 'checkout_initiated': Customer started checkout process

This categorization helps filter and analyze different types of cart changes.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description:
Reason for creating this snapshot. Typically describes what change occurred in the cart.

Examples:
- 'Added product variant Red/Large'
- 'Changed quantity from 2 to 3'
- 'Removed out of stock item'
- 'Customer initiated checkout'
- 'Cart emptied by customer'

This human-readable description provides context for why the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: snapshot_data
plainFields.description:
Complete JSON representation of the shopping cart state at snapshot time.

This field preserves the exact cart structure including:
- Cart items with product names, variant options, and prices
- Quantities and subtotals for each item
- Total cart price and tax calculations
- Applied discounts or promotions
- Cart metadata and timestamps

The JSON structure allows full reconstruction of the cart state for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. This immutable timestamp records exactly when the cart state was captured, enabling chronological audit trails and time-based analysis.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_cart_item_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots of cart item changes for audit trails, preserving quantity and variant selections before modifications.

This table captures the complete state of a cart item at the moment before a change occurs, providing a historical record for dispute resolution and audit compliance. Each snapshot preserves the shopping cart reference, product variant selection, quantity, and price at the time of capture. Snapshots are created automatically when cart items are modified or removed from the cart, ensuring financial transparency and compliance with the platform's Snapshot Principle requirements.

Snapshots cannot be modified or deleted once created, serving as permanent audit trails for shopping cart activity. Administrators can view cart item snapshots to investigate cart manipulation or resolve customer disputes about price changes during shopping sessions.

foreignFields.name: cart_item_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original cart item being snapshotted. {@link ecommerce_mall_cart_items.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_cart_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the shopping cart containing the snapshotted item. {@link ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts.id}

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product variant selected in the cart item at snapshot time. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of the product variant in the cart at the time of snapshot capture. This preserves how many units the customer had selected before modification or removal.

plainFields.name: price_at_time
plainFields.description: Price of the product variant at the moment of snapshot capture. Preserves the exact unit price that was displayed to the customer during their shopping session.

plainFields.name: snapshot_timestamp
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when the captured cart item state existed. This represents the moment before the change that triggered the snapshot creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was created in the system.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_orders
models.description:
Main order headers representing completed purchase transactions. Each order contains a unique order number, total purchase amount, customer reference, and derived overall status based on its order items.

Orders serve as the formal purchase commitment record and basis for all fulfillment activities. They capture the customer's intent to purchase specific items from potentially multiple sellers in a single transaction. The overall order status is dynamically derived from the statuses of individual order items according to business rules defined in section 250.

Order data persists indefinitely for historical and legal record-keeping purposes as specified in section 251. Customers cannot delete orders, ensuring a complete audit trail of all purchase transactions. The shipping address snapshot is preserved immutably with each order to maintain delivery record integrity.

Orders reference the purchasing customer through {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id} and contain multiple order items through {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.order_id}. The overall status provides a high-level view of order progress while individual item statuses enable granular tracking and independent processing.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the purchasing customer's account. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: order_number
plainFields.description: Unique business identifier for the order, used for customer and seller reference throughout the order lifecycle. This number is permanent and never changes once assigned.

plainFields.name: total_price
plainFields.description: Total financial amount of the purchase, calculated as the sum of all order item prices multiplied by their quantities at the time of purchase. This value remains fixed regardless of later price changes.

plainFields.name: overall_status
plainFields.description: High-level order status derived from individual order item statuses according to business rules. Valid values: 'paid' (all items paid), 'shipped' (any item shipped, none delivered), 'delivered' (all items delivered), 'cancelled' (all items cancelled), 'refunded' (all items refunded), 'partially completed' (mixed statuses).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was created after successful payment processing.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was last updated, typically when overall status changes due to item status updates.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was soft-deleted, allowing persistence for legal record-keeping while removing from active views. Orders are never physically deleted per section 251 requirements.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_items
models.description:
Individual purchased product variants within customer orders, representing specific SKU purchases with quantity and preserved purchase price.

Each order item records a customer's purchase of a specific product variant at a particular moment in time, preserving the exact price paid regardless of future price changes. Order items have independent status tracking (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) and serve as the foundation for shipment bundling, cancellation requests, and refund processing.

Order items reference both the parent order ({@link ecommerce_mall_orders}) and the specific product variant ({@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants}) that was purchased. Historical snapshots of product, variant, and seller information at purchase time are preserved through {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_snapshots} for audit and dispute resolution.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Parent order containing this item. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Product variant that was purchased. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units purchased for this variant. Must be greater than 0.

plainFields.name: price_at_purchase
plainFields.description: Price per unit at the time of purchase, preserved immutably for financial records and dispute resolution.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current lifecycle status of this order item. Valid values: 'paid' (payment completed), 'shipped' (seller has shipped), 'delivered' (customer confirmed delivery), 'cancelled' (item was cancelled), 'refunded' (item was refunded).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was created during order placement.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was last updated (status changes, quantity adjustments).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was soft deleted, preserving historical records while removing from active queries.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_snapshots

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent order that was snapshotted. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, indicating when the order state was captured.

plainFields.name: order_number
plainFields.description: The order number at the time of snapshot, preserved for historical reference.

plainFields.name: total_amount
plainFields.description: The total order amount in the currency's smallest unit at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: order_status
plainFields.description: The overall order status at the time of snapshot (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially_completed).

plainFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
plainFields.description: Reference to the customer who placed the order, preserved at snapshot time for historical accuracy.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable preservation of product, variant, and seller data at the exact moment of purchase for each order item.

Captures the complete transactional state including product details, variant configuration, and seller profile information as they existed when the customer completed their purchase. This ensures accurate historical records for dispute resolution, customer service, and financial auditing.

Each snapshot is created once when an order is placed and cannot be modified, preserving the integrity of the purchase transaction. The snapshot links to the specific {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id} and serves as a permanent reference to what was actually purchased.

Three critical data sets are preserved:
1. Product snapshot: Name, description, category, base price
2. Variant snapshot: SKU code, option values (stored in normalized child table), specific price
3. Seller snapshot: Shop name, description, business identity

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the specific order item this snapshot preserves. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: product_name
plainFields.description: Name of the product as it appeared at the moment of purchase. Preserves the exact product name the customer saw and purchased.

plainFields.name: product_description
plainFields.description: Product description text as it appeared at the moment of purchase. Captures the complete product information presented to the customer.

plainFields.name: product_base_price
plainFields.description: Base price of the product at the moment of purchase. This is the product's standard price before any variant-specific pricing.

plainFields.name: variant_sku_code
plainFields.description: SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) code of the specific variant purchased. Unique identifier for the variant configuration.

plainFields.name: variant_price
plainFields.description: Specific price of this variant at the moment of purchase. May differ from the product's base price if the variant has a price override.

plainFields.name: seller_shop_name
plainFields.description: Shop name of the seller as it appeared at the moment of purchase. Preserves the business identity under which the purchase was made.

plainFields.name: seller_shop_description
plainFields.description: Shop description of the seller as it appeared at the moment of purchase. Captures the seller's business information presented to customers.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, which should match the order creation time. Immutable creation timestamp for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was last updated. Since snapshots are immutable, this field remains unchanged after creation but maintains consistency with other business entities.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Although snapshots are typically preserved forever, this field supports consistent deletion patterns across all entities.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_status_changes

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item whose status changed. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}

plainFields.name: from_status
plainFields.description: Status before the change. Valid values: 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded'. This represents the order item's state before the transition.

plainFields.name: to_status
plainFields.description: Status after the change. Valid values: 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded'. This represents the new state of the order item after the transition.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional context explaining why the status change occurred. For example: 'Seller shipped the item', 'Customer confirmed delivery', 'Cancellation approved by seller', 'Refund processed by payment gateway'. This provides human-readable explanation for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the status change was recorded. This represents the exact moment the order item transitioned to the new status.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_shipping_address_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable shipping address snapshots preserved with each order for delivery records.

Captures the exact shipping address at the moment of order creation, including all recipient and location information as specified in address format requirements. This snapshot ensures that delivery information cannot be altered after order placement, providing a permanent record for shipping labels, delivery verification, and dispute resolution.

Each order has exactly one shipping address snapshot created at order creation time. The snapshot includes all address fields required for international shipping: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, and country. These values are preserved exactly as provided by the customer at checkout.

{@link ecommerce_mall_orders}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: The order this shipping address snapshot belongs to. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: recipient_name
plainFields.description: Full name of the person receiving the shipment as provided at checkout.

plainFields.name: recipient_phone
plainFields.description: Phone number for delivery contact as provided at checkout.

plainFields.name: street_address
plainFields.description: Complete street address including building number, street name, and any apartment/suite details.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: City or locality for delivery.

plainFields.name: state_province
plainFields.description: State, province, or region for delivery.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: Postal code or ZIP code for delivery location.

plainFields.name: country
plainFields.description: Country for international shipping.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipping address snapshot was created (order creation time).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last updated (should rarely change as snapshots are immutable).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was soft-deleted for audit purposes.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_address_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable shipping address snapshots preserved with each order for delivery and dispute resolution.

This table stores the complete shipping address as captured at order placement time, following the snapshot principle for financial transparency. Each record contains recipient information and full address components that cannot be modified after order creation, ensuring address changes made by customers post-order do not affect existing orders.

Created in reference to ecommerce_mall_orders.id when an order is placed to preserve the delivery address for fulfillment. The 1:1 relationship ensures each order has exactly one address snapshot that remains unchanged throughout the order lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent order that contains this address snapshot. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}

plainFields.name: recipient_name
plainFields.description: Full name of the person receiving the shipment at the delivery address.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Contact phone number for delivery coordination and order communications.

plainFields.name: street_address
plainFields.description: Primary street address line including building number and street name.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: City or locality name for the delivery address.

plainFields.name: state_province
plainFields.description: State, province, or regional administrative division for the address.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: Postal or ZIP code for mail routing and delivery.

plainFields.name: country
plainFields.description: Country name for international shipping and customs purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this address snapshot was created, typically at order placement time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this address snapshot was last updated. For immutable snapshots, this should match created_at unless system modifications occur.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this address snapshot was soft-deleted, allowing for data retention and recovery. Null indicates active record.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_snapshot_options
models.description:
Normalized key-value storage for product variant option values captured in order item snapshots.

Stores the exact option configuration (e.g., color, size, material) as it existed at the moment of purchase, supporting First Normal Form (1NF) normalization instead of JSON string storage. Each record represents one option name-value pair for a specific order item snapshot.

This table ensures data integrity by preventing duplicate option names per snapshot and enables efficient querying of specific option values across historical orders. Used for preserving product specifications for order history, customer service inquiries, and dispute resolution.

foreignFields.name: order_item_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order item snapshot containing these option values. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_snapshots.id}

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Option name identifying the type of attribute (e.g., 'color', 'size', 'material'). Serves as the key in the key-value pair.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Option value representing the specific attribute selection (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton'). Serves as the value in the key-value pair.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this option value was recorded. Automatically set when the snapshot is created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this option value was last updated. Automatically updated on record modification.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipments
models.description:
Main shipment entity representing a physical package sent by a seller to a customer. Contains tracking information, carrier details, and shipment dates. Serves as the digital-physical fulfillment bridge connecting online orders to physical delivery.

Shipments bundle multiple order items from the same seller with shared tracking information. Each shipment is created by a seller when they dispatch purchased items for delivery. Shipment creation changes the status of all included order items from 'paid' to 'shipped'. Customers can view tracking information and confirm delivery per shipment, not per individual item.

This table tracks carrier information, shipment date, delivery confirmation, and provides the foundation for the shipment lifecycle from creation to delivery confirmation. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers} create shipments for their sold items. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_items} links shipments to specific order items. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_delivery_confirmations} tracks delivery confirmation events.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller who created and dispatched this shipment. All items in a shipment must be from the same seller. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: carrier_name
plainFields.description: Name of the shipping carrier handling the package delivery. Examples include 'USPS', 'FedEx', 'DHL', or local delivery services. Used by customers to identify which carrier to track their package with.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Unique identifier assigned by the carrier for tracking package progress through the delivery system. Customers use this number to monitor shipment status on carrier websites or apps. Must be unique per carrier to ensure accurate tracking.

plainFields.name: shipment_date
plainFields.description: Date and time when the seller dispatched the package for delivery. Marks the beginning of the physical fulfillment process and starts the countdown for automatic delivery confirmation (14 days after this date if not manually confirmed).

plainFields.name: delivered_date
plainFields.description: Date and time when the shipment was confirmed as delivered. Initially null until either the customer confirms delivery or automatic delivery confirmation occurs 14 days after shipment_date. Used to complete the shipment lifecycle.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the shipment lifecycle. Derived from the latest entry in {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_logs}. Common values: 'created', 'in_transit', 'out_for_delivery', 'delivered', 'cancelled'. Helps customers and sellers track shipment progress.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was created in the system. Used for audit trail and chronological ordering of shipments.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was last updated. Tracks modifications to shipment information such as status changes or delivered_date updates.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was soft-deleted. Null indicates the shipment is active; non-null indicates it has been deleted while preserving referential integrity for historical records.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_items
models.description:
Junction table connecting shipments to order items, tracking which specific items are included in each shipment bundle.

Each record represents a specific order item that is part of a physical shipment package. This table enables sellers to bundle multiple order items from the same customer order into a single shipment, reducing shipping costs and simplifying fulfillment. The quantity field tracks how many units of a particular variant are included in the shipment.

Key business rules:
- Each order item can be included in at most one shipment (enforced by unique constraint)
- Shipments can contain multiple order items from the same seller
- Different sellers always ship separately (ensured by application logic, not database constraints)
- Items are moved from 'paid' to 'shipped' status when included in a shipment
- Quantity in shipment must match or be less than order item quantity (validated by application logic)

This table serves as the bridge between digital orders and physical fulfillment, supporting the requirement for customers to confirm delivery per shipment rather than per individual item.

Related entities: {@link ecommerce_mall_shipments}, {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged shipment's {@link ecommerce_mall_shipments.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Included order item's {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units of this order item variant included in the shipment. Must be greater than 0 and cannot exceed the original order item quantity. Used for partial shipments where not all units of an order item are shipped together.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment item record was created, representing when the order item was added to the shipment bundle.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment item record was last updated. Typically updated if quantity is adjusted or item is removed from shipment.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_delivery_confirmations
models.description:
Delivery confirmation records for shipments, tracking when customers confirm delivery and automatic delivery confirmation after timeout period.

Each shipment receives exactly one delivery confirmation record, which is created either manually by the customer confirming receipt or automatically by the system after the configured timeout period (default 14 days). This table supports the requirement that customers confirm delivery per shipment, not per individual order item.

Manual confirmations include a reference to the confirming customer and the exact timestamp when they acknowledged delivery. Automatic confirmations are system-generated when the shipment's shipping date exceeds the auto-confirmation threshold without manual confirmation.

Delivery confirmations trigger status changes for all order items in the shipment, transitioning them from 'shipped' to 'delivered' status. This provides the audit trail required for order fulfillment completion.

{@link ecommerce_mall_shipments} for the shipment being confirmed. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers} for manual confirmations.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_id
foreignFields.description: The shipment being confirmed. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipments.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who manually confirmed delivery, or null for automatic confirmations. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: confirmation_type
plainFields.description: Type of confirmation: 'manual' when customer explicitly confirms delivery, or 'automatic' when system confirms after timeout period.

plainFields.name: confirmed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when delivery was confirmed, either by customer action or system automation.

plainFields.name: shipping_date
plainFields.description: Original shipping date of the shipment, used to calculate automatic confirmation timing. This is copied from the shipment's shipping date at confirmation time for historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: auto_confirmation_days
plainFields.description: Number of days after shipping date when automatic confirmation occurs. Default is 14 days per requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this delivery confirmation record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this delivery confirmation record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this delivery confirmation record was soft deleted, or null if active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots of shipment state changes for audit and dispute resolution, preserving the complete shipment state at specific points in time.

This table captures the exact state of shipments whenever significant changes occur, serving as an audit record for dispute resolution and financial transparency under the platform's Snapshot Principle. Unlike regular entities, snapshot tables store denormalized copies of parent data to preserve historical context while maintaining referential integrity.

Shipment snapshots are created automatically when shipment details are modified or when status changes occur. They provide a complete historical record needed to resolve disputes about delivery timelines, carrier performance, or shipment tracking accuracy. These snapshots are append-only records that cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring a complete audit trail of all shipment modifications throughout the fulfillment process.

Access parent shipment data through the foreign key relationship. Historical shipping addresses are preserved in the separate ecommerce_mall_shipment_snapshot_addresses table to maintain 1NF compliance. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipments.id}

foreignFields.name: shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent shipment entity. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipments.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, representing the exact moment of shipment state capture.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was last updated. For snapshot tables, this typically matches created_at unless corrections are made.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was soft-deleted, if applicable. Null indicates the snapshot is active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_logs
models.description:
Historical log of shipment status transitions throughout the lifecycle from created to delivered or cancelled.

Each record captures a single status change event for a shipment, including the previous status, new status, timestamp, and the actor who initiated the change. This provides a complete audit trail of shipment lifecycle progression and supports dispute resolution, delivery confirmation tracking, and compliance with the platform's financial transparency requirements.

Status transitions are triggered by various system events: shipment creation by sellers, delivery confirmation by customers, automatic timeout deliveries, and administrative interventions. The log preserves the complete history of how each shipment progressed through its lifecycle.

Actor type tracking uses discriminator field 'actor_type' with values: 'seller', 'customer', 'system', 'administrator'. Specific actor references are maintained in separate subtype tables for referential integrity and proper normalization.

{@link ecommerce_mall_shipments}

foreignFields.name: shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the shipment whose status is being logged. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipments.id}.

plainFields.name: previous_status
plainFields.description: The shipment status before this transition occurred. This field preserves the historical state for audit trail purposes and helps reconstruct the exact sequence of status changes.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: The new shipment status after this transition. This represents the updated state of the shipment as recorded at the time of the status change event.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who initiated the status change. Possible values: 'seller', 'customer', 'system', 'administrator'. This identifies which role performed the action that triggered the status transition.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable reason or note explaining why the status change occurred. Used for manual status updates, administrative interventions, or exceptional circumstances that require documentation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status transition was recorded. Represents the exact moment when the shipment changed from the previous status to the new status.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status log record was last updated. Maintains audit trail of modifications to the status log itself.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status log record was soft-deleted. Allows recovery of audit trail data while supporting data retention policies.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_snapshot_addresses
models.description:
Normalized shipping address information for shipment snapshots, storing address components individually to maintain 1NF compliance and avoid JSON string storage.

This table captures the complete shipping address state at the time of shipment creation, including recipient details, phone number for delivery coordination, and full location information.
