Each record preserves the exact address configuration used for a specific shipment, ensuring audit trail integrity and dispute resolution capability.

Address snapshots are immutable and cannot be modified after creation, providing a permanent record of the delivery location as it existed when the shipment was processed. This supports the Snapshot Principle requirement for financial transparency in the shipping process.

{@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_snapshots.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the shipment snapshot containing this address. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_snapshots.id}

plainFields.name: recipient_name
plainFields.description: Full name of the person receiving the package at the delivery address, used by carriers for identity verification and successful delivery completion.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Contact phone number for delivery coordination, allowing carriers to schedule deliveries or resolve delivery issues with the recipient.

plainFields.name: street_address
plainFields.description: Complete physical location details including building number, street name, apartment or unit number, and any specific location identifiers necessary for precise delivery.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: City or municipality where the delivery address is located, used for regional routing and distribution center assignment.

plainFields.name: state_province
plainFields.description: State or province designation for proper regional sorting and carrier territory assignment.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: Postal or zip code enabling precise geographic sorting and delivery area identification for carrier systems.

plainFields.name: country
plainFields.description: Country designation ensuring proper international shipping procedures and customs documentation when applicable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the address snapshot was created, recording the exact moment the address was captured for shipment processing.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the address snapshot was last updated, though typically immutable after creation as required by the Snapshot Principle.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_log_of_sellers
models.description:
Links shipment status logs to seller actors when actor_type is 'seller'. Provides referential integrity and proper relationship normalization for seller-initiated status changes.

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern where shipment_status_logs can have different actor types (seller, customer, administrator). When the actor_type field in shipment_status_logs is 'seller', this table establishes the specific seller relationship. It tracks which seller initiated the status change and includes their session context for audit purposes.

The table maintains a 1:1 relationship with shipment_status_logs to ensure each seller-initiated status log has exactly one seller reference.

foreignFields.name: shipment_status_log_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the shipment status log that was initiated by a seller. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_logs.id}

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller who initiated the status change. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

foreignFields.name: seller_session_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller session at the time of status change initiation. {@link ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this seller status log relationship was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this seller status log relationship was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this seller status log relationship was soft deleted, or null if still active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_log_of_customers
models.description:
Links shipment status logs to customer actors when actor_type is 'customer'. This implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for customer-initiated shipment status changes.

Each shipment status log can have at most one customer actor association, ensuring referential integrity when shipment status changes are initiated by customers. This table provides the customer-specific context for status logs that have actor_type 'customer'.

This is a subsidiary entity that depends on the main {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_logs} table for its existence and is managed through the shipment status log lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: shipment_status_log_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the shipment status log entry. This implements the polymorphic ownership pattern where each status log can have exactly one customer association when actor_type is 'customer'. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_logs.id}

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer actor who initiated the status change. Links to the customer's authentication record for auditing purposes. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this customer-shipment status log association was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this customer-shipment status log association was last updated.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_log_of_administrators
models.description:
Links shipment status logs to administrator actors when actor_type is 'administrator'. Implements the subtype pattern for polymorphic ownership, providing referential integrity and proper relationship normalization for administrator-initiated shipment status changes.

This table connects the main {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_logs} entity to the {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators} actor table, ensuring that administrator actions on shipment status transitions are properly tracked and auditable. The 1:1 relationship with shipment status logs enforces that each status log can have at most one administrator actor reference when the actor_type indicates administrator involvement.

As an append-only audit table, this record is never soft-deleted and serves as a permanent reference for accountability tracking and maintaining referential integrity between shipment status changes and the administrators who initiated them.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_log_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the shipment status log being linked to an administrator. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_status_logs.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator actor who initiated the shipment status change. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this administrator linkage was created. Automatically set when the record is inserted. As an append-only audit table, this timestamp provides chronological ordering of administrator actions.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this administrator linkage was last updated. Automatically updated on record modifications.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewing customer's {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewed product's {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Specific delivered order item that enabled this review. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Star rating from 1 to 5 representing customer satisfaction. Required for every review.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Optional text feedback providing details about product quality, features, or performance.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was last modified. Auto-updated on changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was deleted. Null means review is active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshots of review modifications, preserving previous review states for audit trails and version control.

When a customer edits their review, a snapshot captures the complete review state immediately before the edit. This includes the rating, text content, and metadata. Snapshots are immutable and serve as a permanent audit trail for review modifications, supporting the platform's financial integrity requirements.

Each snapshot is linked to the original review through {@link ecommerce_mall_reviews.id} and records the customer who made the review through {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id} for accountability. The snapshot_reason field documents why the snapshot was created (e.g., 'edit', 'moderation', 'correction').

Snapshots cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring a complete historical record of all review changes for dispute resolution and compliance purposes.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Original review that this snapshot captures. {@link ecommerce_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who authored the original review. Preserved for audit trail even if customer account is deleted. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Review rating from 1 to 5 stars as captured at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Review text content as captured at snapshot time. May be empty if the review had no text content.

plainFields.name: snapshot_reason
plainFields.description: Reason why this snapshot was created, such as 'edit', 'moderation', 'correction', or 'system_update'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, representing the exact moment the review state was captured.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_review_helpful_votes
models.description:
Customer votes on review helpfulness to improve review quality and ranking.

This table tracks which customers have marked which reviews as helpful, creating a social proof system that surfaces valuable reviews to other shoppers. Each vote represents a customer's assessment that a review provided useful information for making purchasing decisions.

The vote system contributes to the marketplace trust ecosystem by allowing customers to collectively identify high-quality reviews. Helpful votes influence review ranking in product detail pages, prioritizing reviews that other customers have found valuable.

A customer can vote each review only once, and votes are immutable once cast. When a customer deletes their account, their votes are preserved to maintain the integrity of the review ranking system. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id} {@link ecommerce_mall_reviews.id}

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who voted the review as helpful. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Review that received the helpful vote. {@link ecommerce_mall_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer voted the review as helpful.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_review_deletions
models.description:
Tracks review deletion events and preserves customer references for audit trail.

When a customer deletes their review, this table records the deletion event with timestamp and preserves the customer's identity even if they later delete their account. This supports the requirement to show deleted reviews as originating from a 'deleted user' while maintaining an audit trail of who performed the deletion.

The table stores the customer's display name and email at the time of deletion, ensuring these details remain available for display and audit purposes regardless of account status changes.

{@link ecommerce_mall_reviews} for the deleted review reference.
{@link ecommerce_mall_customers} for the customer who performed the deletion.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the deleted review. {@link ecommerce_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer who performed the deletion. May be null if customer account is deleted before the review deletion event is recorded. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: customer_display_name
plainFields.description: Customer's display name at the time of review deletion. Preserved even if customer later changes name or deletes account.

plainFields.name: customer_email
plainFields.description: Customer's email address at the time of review deletion. Preserved for audit trail and 'deleted user' display.

plainFields.name: deletion_reason
plainFields.description: Optional reason for deletion provided by the customer. May be null if no reason given.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was deleted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the deletion record was last updated. Initially matches created_at.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_review_order_constraints
models.description:
Enforces the business constraint that customers can write at most one review for a given product within a single order. This table tracks which product-order combinations have already been reviewed to prevent duplicate reviews while allowing reviews of the same product in subsequent orders. The composite unique constraint on customer, order, and product ensures the one-review-per-product-per-order rule is maintained.

This table serves as a constraint mechanism rather than a business entity, providing referential integrity for review creation workflows. It exists solely to enforce the business rule specified in requirements and has no independent lifecycle outside of review creation.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer who wrote the review. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order containing the reviewed product. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product that was reviewed. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the constraint record was created (when the review was first created). This serves as an audit trail for when the product-order combination was first reviewed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the constraint record was last updated. Required for all business entities to track modifications.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the constraint record was soft-deleted, if applicable. Allows for audit trail and potential recovery of constraint records.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_review_states
models.description:
Tracks review lifecycle state transitions including active, edited, and deleted states with timestamps.

This table maintains an audit trail of review state changes to support the snapshot principle and preserve review lifecycle history even after account deletion. Each record represents a specific state that a review has been in at a particular time, enabling historical queries about review status changes.

Relationship: Each state record belongs to a specific {@link ecommerce_mall_reviews.id} and provides chronological tracking of that review's status transitions.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent review. {@link ecommerce_mall_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: state
plainFields.description: Review lifecycle state at the time of this record. Values: 'active' for initial publication, 'edited' for after modifications, 'deleted' for soft deletion while preserving snapshots.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this state was applied to the review. Used for chronological tracking of state transitions.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Optional notes about the state transition, such as reasons for deletion or edit details.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_requests
models.description:
Administrator requests submitted by users wanting to become administrators. Tracks request submissions with reason text, status workflow, and review processing. Any authenticated user (customer or seller) can submit a request to become an administrator. Super administrators review and approve or reject these requests. Duplicate pending requests from the same user are prevented to avoid spamming. When a request is approved, the user becomes a regular administrator with platform management privileges.

The request includes the submission reason, current status, and timestamps for submission and processing. Each request is reviewed by a super administrator who provides approval or rejection. The snapshot principle applies - all status changes create immutable snapshots for audit trails via the {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_request_snapshots} table.

This table serves as the central registry for administrator promotion requests, with subtype tables {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_request_customers} and {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_request_sellers} handling the specific actor relationships using the proper main entity + subtype pattern for polymorphic ownership.

Status field values: 'pending' (awaiting review), 'approved' (request granted), 'rejected' (request denied). Status transitions follow workflow: pending → approved/rejected.

foreignFields.name: reviewing_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Super administrator who reviewed this request. Null while request is pending. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: User-provided reason for requesting administrator privileges. Explains why the user wants to become an administrator and what they intend to contribute to platform management.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the administrator request. 'pending': awaiting review, 'approved': request granted and user promoted to administrator, 'rejected': request denied. Status transitions follow defined workflow rules.

plainFields.name: processed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when a super administrator reviewed and processed this request. Null while request is pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user submitted this administrator request.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this request record was last modified, including status changes and processing updates.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this request was soft deleted. Null if request is active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests
models.description:
Cancellation requests for order items that have not yet shipped, enabling customers to formally request item cancellation with seller approval workflow.

Customers can submit cancellation requests for individual order items with 'paid' status (pre-shipment), providing a reason for the cancellation. Each request is linked to the specific customer submitting it, the order item being requested for cancellation, and the seller responsible for approval decisions.

The request status tracks progression through the approval workflow: 'pending' (awaiting seller response), 'approved' (seller agreed to cancel), or 'rejected' (seller declined). When a seller responds to a cancellation request through {@link ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_responses}, a snapshot is automatically created via {@link ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots} for audit trail purposes.

Approved cancellation requests trigger financial reimbursement to the customer and stock quantity restoration for the cancelled variant via automatic inventory record creation. Rejected requests preserve the seller's decision reason and maintain the order item in its current 'paid' status.

Each order item can have only one active ('pending') cancellation request at any time, preventing duplicate request submissions. Deleted customer accounts preserve their cancellation requests, but are displayed with appropriate anonymization.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who submitted the cancellation request. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item being requested for cancellation. Must have 'paid' status. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller responsible for approving or rejecting the cancellation request. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Customer's explanation for requesting cancellation of the order item. Provides context to help sellers make informed approval decisions.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current state of the cancellation request in the approval workflow. Valid values: 'pending' (awaiting seller response), 'approved' (seller agreed to cancel), 'rejected' (seller declined).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cancellation request was initially submitted by the customer.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cancellation request was last modified, including status changes.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_refund_requests
models.description:
Refund requests for delivered order items within 7-day window. Customers can request refunds for items with 'delivered' status within 7 days of delivery, providing a reason for the request. Sellers can approve or reject the request with optional explanation.

When a refund request is approved, the customer receives financial reimbursement for the specific order item and the stock quantity is restored via inventory record. If rejected, the seller's response reason provides closure to the customer. All decisions create immutable snapshots for audit trails and dispute resolution.

Refund requests follow strict business constraints: 7-day submission window from delivery confirmation, delivered status requirement, one active request per order item, and seller-specific ownership for decision-making. This structured process ensures accountability while supporting post-purchase issue resolution.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who submitted the refund request. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item being requested for refund. Must have 'delivered' status and be within 7-day window from delivery confirmation. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller responsible for evaluating and deciding on the refund request. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Customer's explanation for requesting the refund, describing the specific issue with the delivered item such as damage, incorrect product, quality problems, or unmet expectations.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current state of the refund request in the evaluation workflow. Valid values: 'pending' (awaiting seller response), 'approved' (seller agreed to refund), 'rejected' (seller declined refund).

plainFields.name: seller_response_reason
plainFields.description: Optional explanation provided by the seller when rejecting a refund request, helping customers understand the decision and providing closure.

plainFields.name: delivery_confirmed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order item was confirmed as delivered, used to calculate the 7-day refund eligibility window.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Calculated expiration timestamp representing the deadline for refund request submission (7 days after delivery confirmation). Used for automatic validation of eligibility window.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller approved or rejected the refund request, or when an administrator intervened.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request was submitted by the customer.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request was last modified (status change, seller response, etc.).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request was soft-deleted. Preserved for historical reference while removing from active queries.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_request_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshot records capturing the complete state of administrator request changes for audit trails and historical reference.

When an administrator request's status changes (pending → approved/rejected), a snapshot is automatically created to preserve the previous state. This ensures full transparency in the administrator approval workflow and provides an audit trail for platform management decisions.

Each snapshot contains a denormalized copy of all relevant administrator request fields at the moment of status change, including the request reason, current status, any administrator response, and timestamps. Snapshots cannot be modified or deleted, maintaining the integrity of the administrator approval audit trail.

This table works with {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_requests} to provide comprehensive oversight of the administrator appointment process, supporting platform integrity requirements.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_request_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator request being snapshotted. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: reviewed_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who reviewed the request, if the status has been changed from pending. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The status of the administrator request at the time of snapshot creation. Typically 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the user requesting administrator status, as recorded at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: admin_response
plainFields.description: The response from the reviewing administrator (if any), explaining approval or rejection decision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, recording the exact moment of administrator request state capture.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was last updated. For audit purposes, should typically match created_at as snapshots are immutable.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots

foreignFields.name: cancellation_request_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original cancellation request that this snapshot captures. {@link ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, capturing the exact moment of request state preservation.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshot records capturing the complete state of refund requests at the moment of status changes, preserving previous states for audit trails and dispute resolution.

This table captures the exact state of a refund request whenever a seller responds to it. Each snapshot preserves the refund request's status, customer's reason, seller's response, and all actor references at the moment before the response is processed. Snapshots are created whenever a seller approves or rejects a refund request, ensuring financial transparency and audit compliance as required by the Snapshot Principle.

Snapshots include foreign key references to all related entities (customer, seller, order_item) to provide complete context for independent audit analysis. They are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted, providing a permanent record for dispute resolution and financial auditing.

References the parent {@link ecommerce_mall_refund_requests} and serves as historical documentation of the refund workflow lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: Parent refund request that this snapshot captures. {@link ecommerce_mall_refund_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who submitted the refund request. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller responsible for responding to the refund request. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item being refunded. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: snapshot_status
plainFields.description: Status captured at the moment of snapshot creation. This is the status from the parent refund request at the time the snapshot was taken, preserving the historical state for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: customer_reason
plainFields.description: Customer's reason for requesting a refund, preserved exactly as submitted at the time of snapshot creation. This duplicates the parent's reason field for historical accuracy in audits.

plainFields.name: seller_response_reason
plainFields.description: Seller's response reason captured at snapshot time, if a response existed. Nullable because snapshots may capture pending states before seller response.

plainFields.name: response_status
plainFields.description: Seller's response status at snapshot time (approved, rejected, or null if pending). Captures the decision state for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Represents the exact moment when the refund request state was captured for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was last updated. For snapshots, this should rarely change as they are meant to be immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was marked as deleted. Since snapshots are immutable audit records, this should typically be null unless exceptional administrative action is required.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_responses
models.description:
Seller responses to cancellation requests with decision and explanation.

When a seller receives a cancellation request from a customer for an order item, they must respond with an 'approved' or 'rejected' decision and provide an explanation for their decision. This table records the seller's formal response, which triggers the cancellation workflow and creates a snapshot for audit purposes.

Each response is tied to exactly one cancellation request and records which seller made the decision. The response determines whether the order item will be cancelled and its stock restored, or whether the cancellation request is denied and the order proceeds normally.

This table is part of the financial audit trail required for the platform's money handling. All responses are immutable once created and are referenced in snapshots for dispute resolution.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_id
foreignFields.description: The cancellation request being responded to. {@link ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller who made the response decision. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: decision
plainFields.description: The seller's decision on the cancellation request. Must be either 'approved' or 'rejected'. Approved decisions trigger order item cancellation, refund processing, and stock restoration. Rejected decisions leave the order item in 'paid' status to proceed with shipping.

plainFields.name: explanation
plainFields.description: The seller's explanation for their decision. Provides business context for why the cancellation was approved or rejected, which customers can view and administrators can reference for dispute resolution.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller submitted their response. This records when the decision was made in the cancellation workflow.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the response was last updated. Responses are generally immutable once created, but this field supports potential corrections during the review window.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the response was soft-deleted. Responses should not be deleted under normal circumstances as they are part of the financial audit trail, but this supports exceptional cases.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_refund_request_responses
models.description:
Seller responses to customer refund requests with approval/rejection decisions and explanatory text.

Each refund request for a delivered order item can receive exactly one seller response. The response includes the seller's decision (approve or reject) and an optional explanation. When a seller responds, a snapshot of the refund request state is automatically created as required by the Snapshot Principle. Approved refunds trigger refund processing and restore stock quantities via inventory records.

This table maintains a 1:1 relationship with {@link ecommerce_mall_refund_requests} through the unique foreign key constraint. Each response must be associated with an active seller session for audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: The refund request being responded to. {@link ecommerce_mall_refund_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who made the decision on the refund request. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_session_id
foreignFields.description: Active seller session during the decision. {@link ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions.id}.

plainFields.name: decision
plainFields.description: Seller's decision on the refund request. Must be either 'approved' or 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: explanation
plainFields.description: Optional text explaining the decision rationale. Provides transparency to customers about why refunds were approved or rejected.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller response was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller response was last updated. Typically matches created_at since responses are immutable after creation.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_request_customers
models.description:
Links administrator requests to specific customer actors who submitted them.

Implements the subtype pattern for customer-originated administrator requests with 1:1 relationship to main request table. Each record represents a customer's submission of an administrator request, maintaining the connection between the request and the customer actor for accountability and tracking purposes.

Related to {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_requests} as the main request entity and {@link ecommerce_mall_customers} as the submitting actor.

foreignFields.name: administrator_request_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator request being linked to this customer submission. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer actor who submitted this administrator request. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this customer request submission was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this customer request submission was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this customer request submission was soft-deleted. Null if active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_request_sellers
models.description:
Links administrator requests to specific seller actors who submitted them. Implements the subtype pattern for seller-originated administrator requests with 1:1 relationship to main request table.

This table records which sellers have submitted requests to become administrators, maintaining the connection between the administrator request and the seller actor's identity. The 1:1 constraint ensures each administrator request can have at most one seller origin, while the foreign key to sellers ensures proper actor authentication and identity tracking.

{@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_requests} for the main request being linked.
{@link ecommerce_mall_sellers} for the seller actor who submitted the request.

foreignFields.name: administrator_request_id
foreignFields.description: Main administrator request being linked to a seller. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller actor who submitted the administrator request. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller was linked to this administrator request.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this link record was last updated.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_grades

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator whose grade assignment history is being tracked. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}

foreignFields.name: assigned_by_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator who assigned this historical grade. For initial assignments, this may be the same as administrator_id. For promotions/demotions, this tracks which super administrator performed the action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: assigned_grade
plainFields.description: Historical administrator grade indicating privilege level at assignment time. Must be either 'regular' or 'super'. Captures the grade value at that historical moment, which may differ from current administrator grade. Super administrators have additional privileges including hierarchy management and promotion/demotion authority.

plainFields.name: assigned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this historical grade assignment became effective. For the current active grade, this should match the most recent valid assignment.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this historical grade assignment expires or is superseded. Null indicates this is the current active grade assignment. When a new grade is assigned, the previous grade's expires_at should be set to the new assignment time.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the historical grade assignment, promotion, or demotion. This provides context for hierarchy changes and helps maintain audit trail of administrative decisions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this historical grade assignment record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this historical grade assignment record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this historical grade assignment record was soft deleted. Allows tracking of historical grade assignments while maintaining referential integrity.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_action_logs
models.description:
Log of administrative actions taken across the platform for auditing and oversight.

Records all significant actions performed by administrators including user management (ban/unban), seller approvals/suspensions, product deletions, order interventions, category management, and platform oversight activities. Each log entry captures what action was performed, by which administrator, when, and the target entity affected. This table serves as the primary audit trail for all administrative activities, enabling compliance monitoring, dispute resolution, and historical analysis of platform governance.

Actions are categorized by type and status, with optional metadata providing additional context about the action. The log preserves deleted records via soft delete to maintain complete audit trails even for removed administrative actions.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer affected by the action, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller affected by the action, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Product affected by the action, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Order affected by the action, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Category affected by the action, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative action performed. Examples: 'customer_ban', 'seller_approval', 'product_deletion', 'order_intervention', 'category_management', 'platform_oversight'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of what action was performed, including context and rationale.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Status of the action: 'success' for completed actions, 'failed' for attempted actions that did not complete successfully, 'pending' for actions requiring follow-up.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the action was performed and logged.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the action log entry was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the action log entry was soft-deleted. Null indicates active record.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_seller_suspensions
models.description:
Tracks seller account suspensions enforced by administrators for policy violations or platform integrity concerns.

Administrators can independently create, search, filter, and manage suspension records. When a seller is suspended, their products are hidden from search and category listings, and they cannot create or edit products. However, suspended sellers can still process existing orders including shipping items and responding to cancellation/refund requests.

Each suspension record includes the suspension reason, effective period (with optional end date for temporary suspensions), and the administrator who enforced it. Suspensions can be manually ended by administrators (unsuspension) or automatically expire based on end date.

This table supports the requirement that administrators can suspend and unsuspend seller accounts while preserving the ability for sellers to fulfill existing obligations.

Related entities: {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers} (suspended seller), {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators} (enforcing administrator).

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Suspended seller's identity. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who enforced the suspension. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation for the suspension, providing transparency about policy violations or platform integrity concerns.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current suspension status: 'active' (currently enforced), 'expired' (end date passed), or 'manually_ended' (administrator unsuspended).

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Date and time when the suspension takes effect, marking when seller restrictions begin.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description: Optional end date for temporary suspensions. If null, suspension is indefinite until manually ended.

plainFields.name: ended_at
plainFields.description: Date and time when the suspension was manually ended by an administrator (unsuspension). Null for active or expired suspensions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this suspension record was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this suspension record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this suspension record was soft deleted. Null for active records.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_category_actions
models.description:
Tracks all administrative actions performed on categories for audit and compliance purposes.

This table records when administrators create, edit, delete, archive, or restore categories in the system. Each action includes details about what was changed, who performed the action, and when it occurred. This provides a complete audit trail for category management as required by the Snapshot Principle and platform compliance requirements.

Actions reference the administrator who performed them via {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id} and the affected category via {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id} (when applicable). For category creation actions, the category_id may be null until the category is created, then linked via subsequent update.

All category management operations are captured here, including status transitions between Active, Archived, and Deleted states.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the category action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Category affected by the action. Null for creation actions before category is created. {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative action performed on the category. CREATE for new categories, EDIT for modifications, DELETE for removal, ARCHIVE for hiding, RESTORE for unarchiving.

plainFields.name: action_status
plainFields.description: Status of the action execution. SUCCESSFUL for completed actions, FAILED for errors, PENDING for in-progress operations.

plainFields.name: old_category_name
plainFields.description: Previous category name before EDIT action. Null for CREATE and other non-edit actions.

plainFields.name: new_category_name
plainFields.description: New category name after EDIT action or created name for CREATE action.

plainFields.name: old_category_description
plainFields.description: Previous category description before EDIT action. Null for CREATE and other non-edit actions.

plainFields.name: new_category_description
plainFields.description: New category description after EDIT action or created description for CREATE action.

plainFields.name: old_parent_category_id
plainFields.description: Previous parent category ID before EDIT action that changes hierarchy. Null for CREATE and other non-edit actions.

plainFields.name: new_parent_category_id
plainFields.description: New parent category ID after EDIT action that changes hierarchy. Null for CREATE and other non-edit actions.

plainFields.name: old_status
plainFields.description: Previous category status before status change action. One of: ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, DELETED.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: New category status after status change action. One of: ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, DELETED.

plainFields.name: failure_reason
plainFields.description: Error message or reason when action_status is FAILED. Null for successful actions.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address of the administrator when performing the action for security auditing.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string of the administrator's browser/device for audit trail.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrative action was initiated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the action record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft deletion of the action record. Null for active records.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_product_deletions
models.description:
Administrative product deletion records for policy violations, preserving deletion reasons and timestamps for audit purposes.

This table captures when administrators delete products from the platform for policy violations or other administrative reasons. Each record includes the administrator who performed the deletion, the product being deleted, the reason for deletion, and timestamps. These records serve as an audit trail for platform oversight and ensure accountability for product removals.

The deletion reason is required and provides justification for the action, which can be reviewed by other administrators or used for dispute resolution. Records are immutable and cannot be modified after creation to maintain audit integrity.

{@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id} for administrator accountability
{@link ecommerce_mall_products.id} for the product being deleted

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the product deletion. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Product that was deleted by the administrator. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

plainFields.name: deletion_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the administrative product deletion, providing justification for the action.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrative deletion record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrative deletion record was last updated.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_order_interventions
models.description:
Tracks administrative order interventions where administrators can force-cancel or force-refund order items or entire orders.

This table records all platform administrator interventions on orders, including force cancellations (refunds customer and restores stock) and force refunds. Each intervention captures the administrator who performed it, the target order and optional specific order item, intervention type, reason for the action, and execution status for auditing purposes.

These records serve as an audit trail for platform integrity enforcement and are referenced in administrative oversight logs. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id} identifies the administrator who performed the intervention, while {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id} and optionally {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id} identify the affected order and specific item.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the intervention. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Target order affected by the intervention. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Specific order item targeted (nullable for order-level interventions). {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: intervention_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative intervention: 'force_cancel' for pre-shipment cancellations with refund, or 'force_refund' for post-delivery refunds.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Administrator's reason or justification for the intervention, required for audit trail and transparency.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Execution status of the intervention: 'pending' for scheduled actions, 'executing' for in-progress, 'completed' for successful execution, or 'failed' for unsuccessful attempts.

plainFields.name: executed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the intervention was actually executed (processing completed).

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Error message if the intervention failed during execution, null for successful interventions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the intervention record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the intervention record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the intervention record was soft deleted (for audit trail preservation).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_customer_bans
models.description:
Customer account ban records tracking ban periods, reasons, and administrative oversight.

This table records administrative actions where customers are banned from the platform. Each ban includes the administrator who imposed the ban, the customer who was banned, the effective period of the ban, the reason for the ban, and the current status. Bans can be temporary (with an expiration date) or indefinite (no expiration). When a customer is banned, they cannot log in or access the platform until the ban is lifted.

Administrators can view all active bans, search by customer or administrator, and manage ban status. The ban status tracks whether the ban is currently active, has expired, or has been manually revoked by an administrator. Ban records are preserved for audit purposes even after they expire or are revoked.

Bans affect customer login capabilities and platform access. When a ban is active, the customer's login attempts are blocked. When a ban expires or is revoked, the customer can resume normal platform access.

Related tables: {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators} (who performed the ban), {@link ecommerce_mall_customers} (who was banned).

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who imposed the ban. This references the administrator who took the action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who was banned. This references the customer account that is subject to the ban. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: ban_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the ban as entered by the administrator. This provides justification for the administrative action and is visible to other administrators for oversight. Should be clear and specific to support audit requirements.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the ban. Values: 'active' (ban is currently in effect), 'expired' (ban period has ended), 'revoked' (administrator manually lifted the ban before expiration).

plainFields.name: effective_from
plainFields.description: Date and time when the ban becomes effective. This is typically when the administrator creates the ban record, but can be set to a future date for scheduled bans.

plainFields.name: effective_until
plainFields.description: Date and time when the ban expires. If null, the ban is indefinite (no expiration). For temporary bans, this defines the ban duration. After this date, the status automatically changes to 'expired'.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: Date and time when an administrator manually revoked the ban before its expiration. Null if the ban has not been revoked. When set, the status should be 'revoked'.

plainFields.name: revoked_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for revoking the ban, if applicable. This provides audit trail for why a ban was lifted before its expiration date.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this ban record was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this ban record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this ban record was soft-deleted. Null if not deleted. Allows administrators to remove ban records from active views while preserving audit history.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_platform_oversight_logs
models.description:
Audit log of all platform oversight actions performed by administrators for compliance monitoring and accountability.

This table records every oversight action taken by administrators across the platform, including seller management, customer account oversight, product oversight, category management, and order interventions. Each record captures who performed the action, what action was taken, which entity was affected, and the outcome. These logs serve as an immutable audit trail for compliance monitoring, dispute resolution, and platform integrity verification.

Records in this table are never modified or deleted, providing a complete historical record of all administrative oversight activities as required by the Snapshot Principle and financial audit requirements.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the oversight action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Target seller affected by the oversight action, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Target customer affected by the oversight action, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_product_id
foreignFields.description: Target product affected by the oversight action, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_category_id
foreignFields.description: Target category affected by the oversight action, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}.

foreignFields.name: target_order_id
foreignFields.description: Target order affected by the oversight action, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of oversight action performed. Valid values: 'seller_suspension', 'seller_unsuspension', 'customer_ban', 'customer_unban', 'product_deletion', 'category_creation', 'category_modification', 'category_deletion', 'order_force_cancellation', 'order_force_refund', 'seller_approval', 'seller_rejection', 'administrator_promotion', 'administrator_demotion'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of the oversight action, explaining what was done and why.

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: Detailed information about the action, including any specific parameters, values changed, or additional context. This field may contain structured data in JSON format to capture complex action details.

plainFields.name: outcome
plainFields.description: Result or outcome of the oversight action. Valid values: 'success', 'failed', 'partial_success', 'pending', 'cancelled'.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the oversight action was performed, for security auditing purposes.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string of the browser or client used to perform the oversight action, for client identification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the oversight action was recorded. This represents when the action actually occurred in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the oversight action record was last updated. For audit logs, this should rarely change once created.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_decision_snapshots
models.description: string

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who made the decision. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: decision_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative decision being recorded. Valid values: 'seller_approval', 'seller_suspension', 'seller_unsuspension', 'product_deletion', 'category_action', 'order_intervention', 'customer_ban', 'customer_unban', 'administrator_promotion', 'administrator_demotion', 'platform_integrity_action'.

plainFields.name: target_entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity affected by the decision. Valid values: 'seller', 'customer', 'product', 'category', 'order_item', 'administrator', 'platform'.

plainFields.name: target_entity_id

plainFields.name: decision_outcome

plainFields.name: decision_reason
plainFields.description: Administrator's reason or justification for the decision. Provides context for why the action was taken, which may be referenced during disputes or compliance reviews.

plainFields.name: decision_notes
plainFields.description: Additional notes or details about the decision that may be relevant for historical context or future reference.

plainFields.name: before_state_json
plainFields.description: JSON representation of the target entity's state before the decision was made. Captures relevant attributes and values that existed prior to the administrative action.

plainFields.name: after_state_json
plainFields.description: JSON representation of the target entity's state after the decision was made. Captures the resulting state following the administrative action.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision snapshot was created. This represents when the administrative decision was formally recorded in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision snapshot was last updated. While snapshots are typically immutable, this field tracks any metadata updates.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_access_logs

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who performed the access activity. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}

foreignFields.name: session_id
foreignFields.description: The session associated with this access activity, if applicable. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: activity_type
plainFields.description: Type of access activity performed, such as 'login_attempt', 'session_renewal', 'logout', 'failed_authentication', 'password_change', or 'access_denied'.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the access activity originated, supporting geo-location analysis and IP-based security controls.

plainFields.name: user_agent

plainFields.name: success

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_users
models.description:
Links administrator users to their current administrator grade assignments.

This table establishes which users (from the administrator actor table) have administrator privileges and what grade (regular or super administrator) they currently hold. Each administrator can have only one active grade assignment at a time, tracked through this relationship table. When administrators are promoted or demoted, new records are created to maintain historical tracking of grade changes.

The relationship is essential for enforcing the administrator hierarchy where super administrators have additional privileges including the ability to promote/demote other administrators. This table serves as the authoritative source for determining an administrator's current grade and associated permissions within the platform.

{@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id} references the administrator user identity, while {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_grades.id} references the specific grade configuration currently assigned to that administrator.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator user identity. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: administrator_grade_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator grade configuration currently assigned. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_grades.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this grade assignment was created, typically when an administrator is initially assigned a grade or promoted/demoted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this grade assignment was last updated, useful for tracking recent changes to administrator privileges.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_promotion_histories
models.description:
Historical records of administrator grade changes including promotion and demotion actions.

Tracks when administrators are promoted from regular to super administrator status or demoted from super to regular administrator status. Each record includes the administrator being changed, the administrator performing the change, previous and new grades, reason for the change, and timestamp for audit purposes.

Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super status and demote other super administrators to regular status. Super administrators cannot demote themselves as enforced by business rules. Historical records are immutable and serve as an audit trail for administrator hierarchy management.

foreignFields.name: target_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator whose grade is being changed. References {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: performing_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator performing the grade change. References {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: previous_grade
plainFields.description: Previous administrator grade before the change. Valid values are 'regular' for regular administrator or 'super' for super administrator.

plainFields.name: new_grade
plainFields.description: New administrator grade after the change. Valid values are 'regular' for regular administrator or 'super' for super administrator.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the grade change, explaining why the promotion or demotion was performed. Provides context for audit trail and historical reference.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the grade change record was created. This represents when the promotion or demotion action occurred.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the grade change record was last updated. Since historical records are typically immutable, this usually matches created_at unless corrections are made.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_review_logs
models.description:
Detailed logs of administrator review activities including approvals, rejections, and decisions. This table serves as a comprehensive audit trail for all administrative review actions across the platform.

Records include seller registration approvals/rejections, seller suspension/unsuspension actions, administrator promotions/demotions, category management, product deletions, order interventions, customer bans, and administrator request reviews. Each log entry captures the administrator's decision, reason, and related session context for full accountability and historical reference.

Logs are immutable once created and form part of the platform's integrity assurance system as described in section 25 (Policy Enforcement and Platform Integrity).

foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the review action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: administrator_session_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator session during which the review was performed. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_sessions.id}.

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity being reviewed. Valid values: 'seller_registration', 'seller_suspension', 'administrator_promotion', 'category', 'product', 'order', 'customer_ban', 'administrator_request'.

plainFields.name: entity_id
plainFields.description: ID of the entity being reviewed. References the primary key of the corresponding entity table.

plainFields.name: decision_type
plainFields.description: Type of decision made. Valid values: 'approved', 'rejected', 'suspended', 'unsuspended', 'promoted', 'demoted', 'created', 'edited', 'deleted', 'banned', 'unbanned', 'force_cancelled', 'force_refunded'.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided for the decision. Required for rejections and suspensions, optional for other decision types.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review log entry was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review log entry was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review log entry was soft-deleted, if applicable.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_decision_records
models.description:
Individual decision records capturing administrator reasoning and justification for actions across the platform.

This table serves as the central audit trail for all administrator decisions, including seller approvals/rejections, seller suspensions, product deletions, order interventions, customer bans, category management actions, and administrator promotions/demotions. Each record preserves the complete context of a decision: who made it, when, why, what entity was affected, and what the outcome was.

Decision records support platform integrity by documenting justification for enforcement actions and providing transparency for dispute resolution. They reference specific administrative action tables while maintaining a separate audit trail of the decision-making rationale. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_users.id} identifies the administrator who made the decision, while various foreign keys reference the affected entities and related action records.

foreignFields.description: Administrator who made the decision. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: reviewed_by_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who reviewed the decision (for multi-level approval workflows). {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_suspension_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to specific seller suspension action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_seller_suspensions.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_deletion_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to specific product deletion action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_product_deletions.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_intervention_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to specific order intervention action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_order_interventions.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_ban_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to specific customer ban action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_customer_bans.id}.

foreignFields.name: category_action_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to specific category management action. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_category_actions.id}.

foreignFields.name: administrator_promotion_history_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to specific administrator promotion/demotion history. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_promotion_histories.id}.

foreignFields.name: affected_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller affected by the decision. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: affected_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product affected by the decision. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: affected_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item affected by the decision. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: affected_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer affected by the decision. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: affected_category_id
foreignFields.description: Category affected by the decision. {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}.

foreignFields.name: affected_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator affected by the decision (for promotions/demotions). {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_users.id}.

plainFields.name: decision_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative decision being recorded. Values include: seller_approval, seller_rejection, seller_suspension, seller_unsuspension, product_deletion, order_force_cancellation, order_force_refund, customer_ban, customer_unban, category_creation, category_edition, category_deletion, administrator_promotion, administrator_demotion.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Detailed justification and reasoning for the administrative decision. This field captures the administrator's explanation for the action taken, including policy references, evidence, and business rationale.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the decision. Values: pending_review (awaiting review by another administrator), approved (decision approved for implementation), rejected (decision rejected during review), implemented (decision successfully executed), cancelled (decision cancelled before implementation).

plainFields.name: reference_url
plainFields.description: Optional URL reference to supporting evidence, documentation, or external records that informed the decision. Used for providing additional context or proof for enforcement actions.

plainFields.name: review_notes
plainFields.description: Comments and notes from the reviewing administrator during multi-level approval workflows. Captures feedback, questions, or additional requirements for the decision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision record was initially created. This represents when the administrator first proposed or documented the decision.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision record was last modified. Updated whenever the status, reason, or other fields are changed.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision was reviewed by another administrator. Null until review occurs in multi-level approval workflows.

plainFields.name: implemented_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision was successfully implemented and executed. Null until the associated administrative action is completed.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_customer_ban_snapshots
models.description:
Snapshot records of customer ban modifications for audit trail and historical reference.

This table preserves previous states when customer bans are created, modified, revoked, or deleted by administrators. Each snapshot captures the complete state of a customer ban at a specific point in time, including ban reason, status, effective dates, and administrative metadata. Snapshots are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted once created, ensuring a complete audit trail for compliance and dispute resolution.

Snapshots are created automatically whenever an administrator modifies a customer ban, including initial creation, status changes, reason updates, or deletion. The snapshot preserves the values before the change, allowing historical reconstruction of ban states. For ban deletions, the final state before deletion is captured.

This table supports the platform's financial integrity requirements by providing transparent tracking of all customer account restrictions and administrative actions affecting user access.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_customer_ban_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer ban record that was modified. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_customer_bans.id}.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the ban modification. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the customer ban as recorded at the time of snapshot creation. This captures the administrative justification for the ban action.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Ban status at the time of snapshot creation. Common values include 'active', 'suspended', 'revoked', or 'pending_review'. This preserves the operational state of the ban.

plainFields.name: banned_from
plainFields.description: Effective start date of the ban period as recorded in the snapshot. This preserves when the ban was scheduled to begin taking effect.

plainFields.name: banned_until
plainFields.description: Scheduled end date of the ban period as recorded in the snapshot. Null indicates an indefinite or permanent ban. This preserves the intended duration at the time of the ban modification.

plainFields.name: snapshot_metadata
plainFields.description: Additional contextual metadata about the snapshot creation, such as system context, change type (create, update, delete), or administrative notes. Used for detailed audit trail analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was created. This represents when the ban state was captured for historical preservation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was last updated. For immutable snapshots, this typically matches created_at unless metadata corrections are applied.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_administrator_action_log_metadata
models.description:
Key-value metadata storage for administrator action logs, normalizing additional JSON data into separate table for First Normal Form (1NF) compliance.

Each administrator action log can have multiple metadata key-value pairs that provide additional context or structured data about the administrative action. This table stores those pairs in normalized form rather than as JSON strings in the main action log table, ensuring proper database normalization and query capabilities.

Metadata examples might include: request payload details, affected entity identifiers, action-specific parameters, or system context information that supplements the main log entry.

This table is managed indirectly through administrator action log operations and provides supporting data for audit trails and administrative oversight. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_action_logs}

foreignFields.name: administrator_action_log_id
foreignFields.description: Associated administrator action log. {@link ecommerce_mall_administrator_action_logs.id}

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Metadata key identifying the type of additional data stored. Examples: 'affected_user_id', 'policy_rule', 'request_payload', 'system_context'.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Metadata value associated with the key. Contains the actual data in string format, which can represent identifiers, JSON strings, or other structured information.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this metadata record was created. Automatically set when the metadata is added to an action log.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this metadata record was last updated. Updated whenever metadata values are modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this metadata record was soft-deleted. Null indicates the metadata is active and not deleted.
